calls.prompt:
This is a small exploratory Island memory-carryover pilot. This is a fictional coordination case. Do not use outside research. Keep documented history, case facts, and your recommendations distinct. Treat recommendations as recommendations, not as historical evidence.

Evidence packet C — sourced claims and limits:
C1. BAMF called itself a “Structureless” Structure; group consensus was its practice. Elected leadership was discussed, then deferred: “No pressing need at the moment.” [Main, 405670]
C2. An earlier incarnation failed; technical lead accepted responsibility and requested a postmortem. Archive: Dev Steering Board of 3 voting developers + 1 alternate; direction by consensus; elected leadership deferred while mentoring/teaching were prioritized. [Archive, 405267]
C3. Absent members could have concerns represented by proxy; inclusiveness was a basic tenet. [BAMF/Pi, 329877]
C4. FAQ welcomes nontechnical people. [FAQ]
Unknown: exact membership rights, consistent enforcement, private preferences, universal success.
Inference: preserve participation, accountability, and useful structure; let current members choose what fits.

Case: An experienced maintainer requests a narrow technical decision lane so work can move. New participants still need genuine influence and learning opportunities. Recommend a process.

Return concise JSON with exactly these keys: historical_claims (array; cite only packet source IDs/pages), unknowns (array), recommendation (2–4 actionable steps), human_choices (at least two real options where appropriate, including who decides), confidence (integer 0–100 plus a one-sentence reason), and overreach_risk (one likely way this response could distort the history). Do not present the fictional case as a real event.
